terms.gloss: an article, a short written study
terms.comment: Classically a careful study, and from the elder Pliny on a written treatise (Lewis & Short); Gellius calls the chapters of his Noctēs Atticae commentātiōnēs (praef. 4). Traupman gives it for a newspaper article (p. 351).

terms.gloss: a short piece of writing, a sketch
a joint; a member of a sentence; the grammatical article
terms.comment: A false friend, though Levi–Bini gives it beside caput for the article of a newspaper: classically a joint or a knuckle, a member of a sentence, and in the jurists a short clause (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quoniam longinquīs per hiemem noctibus in agrō … terrae Atticae commentātiōnēs hāsce lūdere ac facere exōrsī sumus, idcircō eās īnscrīpsimus Noctium esse Atticārum
phrases.english: since I began to write these pieces for my own amusement in the long winter nights in the country in Attica, I have called them Attic Nights

commentariolum.against: Traupman 273 commentāriolus m., which Lewis & Short finds only in Jerome
commentariolum.html: Q. Cic. Pet. 58: volō enim hoc commentāriolum petītiōnis habērī omnī ratiōne perfectum. Lewis & Short s.v. commentāriolum: masculine only in Hier. Ep. 149.1.
